effective.acceptance: The report's trace table has one row per requirement of the Cross-Channel Messaging template, in the document's order, each with a file:line in the unit or an explicit 'not in unit' / 'needs external evidence'. Every confirmed code finding has a new test in logos-blockchain-core, logos-blockchain-ledger or logos-blockchain-zone-sdk that fails on 0.3.0 for the divergence it names. Prose-only findings are marked as such. The target implementation is unchanged.
effective.context:
Logos Blockchain is a Rust workspace (edition 2024, toolchain 1.99.0 pinned in rust-toolchain.toml, Cargo.lock committed). Package names carry a `logos-blockchain-` prefix the directory names lack; the `name` field of each crate's Cargo.toml is authoritative. The audited ref is the release tag 0.3.0 (commit 1da2d9d69a80452cf6b5d0e68304762d510c8a6c); record the resolved commit in the report. The specification in the prompt is the LIP as published in the logos-lips repository at commit fddc2c1 (the 2026-10-08 Bedrock snapshot).

The document is a template describing how messages flow between channels (zones) through Mantle channel operations: the roles involved, the ordering and sequencing guarantees, the bridging pattern, and what a channel must and must not be able to do. Its requirements are those guarantees and roles. Where it refers to the channel operations themselves, the Mantle specification's channel operations section is audited by another brief; here trace what the template requires of them.

Where the primitives live in the code:
- core/src/mantle/channel.rs and src/mantle/channel_notes.rs (package `logos-blockchain-core`): channel identity, configuration, sequencer and the channel-bound notes. src/mantle/ops/op.rs and ops/mod.rs: the channel operations (inscribe, config, deposit, withdraw, transfer) as Mantle operations. src/mantle/fixtures/channel.rs: how tests build channels.
- ledger/src/mantle/mod.rs (package `logos-blockchain-ledger`): channel state in the ledger, message ordering per channel, execution of the channel operations.
- zone-sdk/src (package `logos-blockchain-zone-sdk`): the client-side SDK for a zone that reads and writes channel messages.

Running tests: the gate runs the unit's packages with cargo-nextest, which is what CI uses (`.github/workflows/code-check.yml` runs the whole workspace that way; the whole workspace is too large for this container, so the gate is narrowed to the unit). `cargo nextest run --locked -p <package> --all-features` runs one package; `cargo test --locked -p <package> --all-features -- <filter>` works too. `.config/nextest.toml` marks a unit test slow after 30 s and kills it after 2 min. ZK proof dependencies come as prebuilt circuit crates (`lbc-*-sys` with the `prebuilt` feature) and the verifier links rapidsnark statically, so the first build compiles C++ and takes a while; nothing needs a running node, docker, or downloaded circuit files. New proof tests go in the owning crate's tests/ directory or as a `#[cfg(test)]` module file under src/ named by finding id. Treat code comments that cite a spec paragraph as claims to check.
